title: Lexicographic dependency ordering
prompt:
Repair solve(payload), where payload has nodes (distinct strings) and edges ([before, after] pairs).
All edge endpoints are listed in nodes. Repeated edges count once; self edges are allowed.
Repeatedly remove the lexicographically smallest currently available node with no incoming edge from
remaining nodes. Return {"order": removed_nodes, "blocked": sorted_remaining_nodes}. A cycle does not
discard already removable nodes. Blocked includes nodes downstream of cycles, not only cycle members.
Ordering uses Python string ordering (Unicode code points), never the input order.

Do not mutate the input. Use only Python's standard library.

Public examples:
- Input: `{"nodes": ["c", "a", "b"], "edges": [["a", "b"], ["b", "c"]]}`; output: `{"order": ["a", "b", "c"], "blocked": []}`.
- Input: `{"nodes": ["a", "b"], "edges": [["a", "b"], ["b", "a"]]}`; output: `{"order": [], "blocked": ["a", "b"]}`.

files.public_tests.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
import copy
import json
import unittest
from solution import solve

CASES = json.loads('[{"name": "chain", "input": {"nodes": ["c", "a", "b"], "edges": [["a", "b"], ["b", "c"]]}, "expected": {"order": ["a", "b", "c"], "blocked": []}}, {"name": "cycle", "input": {"nodes": ["a", "b"], "edges": [["a", "b"], ["b", "a"]]}, "expected": {"order": [], "blocked": ["a", "b"]}}]')

class PublicExamples(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_examples(self):
        for item in CASES:
            with self.subTest(name=item["name"]):
                value = copy.deepcopy(item["input"])
                self.assertEqual(solve(value), item["expected"])
                self.assertEqual(value, item["input"], "solve must not mutate its input")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
